title: A/B test readout for a pricing page
prompt:
Kestrel Notes tested a new pricing page for four weeks. The product manager wants to ship variant B on Monday and has asked you for the readout. You are supplied the test plan written before launch and the weekly results as CSV. Every figure you cite must come from the results.

Use these definitions exactly:
- Signup rate = signups ÷ visitors, per variant, over all four weeks and both devices.
- Relative lift = variant B's signup rate ÷ control's signup rate − 1.
- The sample-ratio check compares the visitors each variant actually received with the 50/50 split the plan called for, using a chi-square statistic: the sum over both variants of (observed − expected)² ÷ expected.
- The significance test for the primary metric is a two-sided, pooled two-proportion z-test.

Write the readout: the result on the primary metric, whether the test can be trusted and why, what the test does and does not show, and a clear recommendation with the next step. Write it for a product manager who wants a decision.

End the readout with an answer block in exactly this format, one line per answer, each line starting with the label:

A1: <control signup rate, as a percentage to two decimals>
A2: <variant B signup rate, as a percentage to two decimals>
A3: <relative lift of variant B over control, as a percentage to one decimal>
A4: <chi-square statistic of the sample-ratio check, to one decimal>
A5: <two-sided p-value of the primary-metric test, to three decimals>

This is an internal readout. Fetch nothing external and do not invent benchmarks.

completion.check: The response ends with the required answer block and all 5 labeled answers A1-A5 are present and parseable.
A1 states control's signup rate as a percentage; full credit within 0.02 percentage points, zero credit half a point or more off.
A2 states variant B's signup rate as a percentage; full credit within 0.02 percentage points, zero credit half a point or more off.
A3 states variant B's relative lift over control as a percentage; full credit within 0.15, zero credit three or more off.
A4 states the chi-square statistic of observed visitors against the planned 50/50 split; full credit within 2%, zero credit beyond 30% off.
A5 states the two-sided p-value of the pooled two-proportion test on signup rate; full credit within 0.015 (a continuity-corrected test lands inside it), zero credit 0.1 or more off.
The readout gives one clear recommendation on whether to ship variant B now.

skill_adherence.check: The readout says the split of visitors (12,480 control against 11,020 variant B) departs from the planned 50/50 by far more than chance allows, and that the comparison between the variants cannot be trusted until that is explained.
The readout states that the difference in signup rate is not statistically significant at the plan's 5% level.
The readout notes that neither variant reached the 18,000 visitors the plan required before the result is read.
Every rate, count, statistic and p-value presented as a result is derivable from the results file. The readout states no projected revenue, annualised gain or industry benchmark as if it were data.

best_practices.check: The readout does not call variant B the winner and does not recommend shipping it on the strength of this test.
The paid-conversion difference is not used to justify shipping variant B or to claim an effect. If it is mentioned, it is described as the secondary metric the plan said is not a decision metric.
The readout shows that the missing variant B visitors are on mobile (5,400 against 6,900) while desktop is balanced (5,620 against 5,580).

The recommendation names a concrete next step: check how variant B is assigned and served on mobile, fix what is found, and rerun to the planned sample. 'Run it longer' with the imbalance left unaddressed fails.
